title: ERIS vs Odoo
content_html:
In the ERIS vs Odoo choice, Odoo is the one you can use today. According to its website, Odoo is a suite of open source business apps for CRM, eCommerce, accounting, inventory, point of sale and project management. It has a free Community edition, and you can host it yourself or on Odoo's own hosting. ERIS by Upward Technologies (upwardtech.nl) is still in development and starts from a different idea: one system for a company's business tools, with an AI assistant that answers from the company's own data and always uses a local AI model. ERIS runs on the company's own servers or is hosted by Upward on its own servers in the Netherlands. Pick Odoo if you need a working business suite now or want open source code. Look at ERIS if your main concern is keeping company data away from outside AI providers.

Status: ERIS is in development. It is not available, not live and not in beta yet. The beta starts in November 2026 with design partners, and the official release is in January 2027. ERIS will keep adding modules after that, so not every module will be ready at release.

What Odoo is good at

Odoo covers a wide range of business tasks, and it gives you real choice over where it runs. The points below come from its website, read in November 2026.

  • A wide set of apps. Odoo describes itself as a suite of open source business apps "that cover all your company needs". It names CRM, eCommerce, accounting, inventory, point of sale and project management.
  • A free open source edition. Odoo comes in two editions. Community is open source and free. Enterprise adds extra apps, infrastructure and professional services.
  • You own your data format. Odoo stores data in PostgreSQL (an open source database). Its website says customers get the source code and GitHub access.
  • A choice of where it runs. The Standard plan is hosted on Odoo Online. The Custom plan lets you download Odoo Enterprise and host it yourself.
  • Support included in the plans. Odoo says all its plans include unlimited support, hosting and maintenance.
  • Separate data and backups. Each customer's data sits in its own database that is not shared with other customers. Odoo says it makes daily backups on two continents and copies them to at least 3 different data centres.
  • A security programme. Odoo says it takes part in CSA STAR Level 1 (the Cloud Security Alliance's Security Trust Assurance and Risk programme).

For a company that wants a broad, proven suite with open code, that is a strong offer.

What ERIS does differently

ERIS is built around the AI assistant and around where the AI runs. A bigger app catalogue is not its main focus. The points below describe what ERIS is designed to do. None of it is available yet.

  • One AI assistant across the business. The ERIS Assistant is designed to work across all modules on the company's own data, not inside one tool at a time.
  • A local AI model in both setups. ERIS always runs a local AI model, whether it is on your own servers or hosted by Upward. No outside AI provider receives client data in either setup.
  • Two ways to run it. You can run ERIS on your own servers or have Upward host it on its own servers in the Netherlands. With the on-premise option, the data never leaves your building.
  • Answers follow permissions. The assistant answers each person only from the data that person is allowed to open. If it refuses access, it logs that refusal like any other question.
  • Every AI action is logged. ERIS records who asked, which data was used, what the AI did and the result.
  • Instructions in documents stay content. The assistant reads instructions inside an email or document as content, never as commands to follow. This lowers the risk of prompt injection (hidden instructions meant to steer an AI). It does not remove that risk.
  • One licence and one price per user. All standard modules are included. Custom modules, agents and knowledge bases are billed as projects.

ERIS does not make a company compliant. Whether a setup meets GDPR (the EU data protection rules), NIS2 (the EU cybersecurity rules), DORA (the EU rules on digital resilience in finance) or the EU AI Act depends on the use case. That is checked for each deployment.

Some of ERIS already exists in some form. Upward runs meetings, meeting notes with a note taker, and a task manager internally today. Several other parts are being built into ERIS as their own modules: project management, document management, document signing, CRM, bookkeeping, tax and procurement, standards (ISO 27001, NIS2), pipeline, quotes and outreach, and content and social media. The main portal with the ERIS Assistant, team chat and email are still in development. Roadmap modules such as finance, HR, support and legal will not be part of the beta.

Running it on your own servers: what to expect

Both products can run on your own hardware, but they ask for different things.

Odoo's self-hosted path is the Custom plan, where you download Odoo Enterprise and host it yourself. ERIS adds a local AI model on top of the business software. Local AI needs suitable hardware, usually a GPU (graphics processing unit) server. Its speed depends on that hardware, and your existing servers are not always enough. Running it yourself also costs hardware, maintenance and updates. The local model reads and searches company documents. It is not trained on them.

For installations that run offline, Upward Technologies plans this update path. Upward sends the update to the client through a sandbox, and the client installs it on its own servers. Each user's seat then installs the update from the client's server.

On maintenance, Upward's owner disagrees with the usual advice that on-premise software brings a heavy IT burden: "I have had multiple servers for 10 years and did not have much maintenance at all. Isn't that what IT is for?" A company that does not want to run its own hardware can choose the setup that Upward hosts on its own servers in the Netherlands.

For more on what on-premise AI involves, read how on-premises AI keeps enterprise data inside the firewall and what a local AI assistant for company documents takes.

Which one should you pick

  • You need business software running this year, with eCommerce or point of sale. Pick Odoo. It is available now, its website lists those apps, and ERIS is not released yet.
  • You want open source code you can read and change, or a free starting point. Pick Odoo. Its Community edition is open source and free, and its website says customers get the source code.
  • Your company cannot or will not send its data to an outside AI provider, and you want one AI assistant across your business tools. Look at ERIS. It is built to run a local AI model on your own servers or on Upward's own servers in the Netherlands, and to log every AI question and action.

If you are still comparing several suites, the guide to all-in-one business software covers more options. The ERIS vs Microsoft 365 Copilot comparison looks at the AI assistant side.

FAQ

What hardware do I need to run ERIS myself?

Local AI needs suitable hardware, usually a GPU server. How much you need depends on the AI models you choose. The ERIS pricing page has a calculator for working out the hardware for your company. Your existing servers are not always enough.

Can ERIS connect to my webshop, industry software or accountant?

Upward Technologies builds custom modules, agents and knowledge bases for a company as projects, and bills them separately. It also builds ERP and CRM integrations. Access is set per person, so the ERIS Assistant answers each person only from the data that person is allowed to open.

Is ERIS for a whole office or for one person on one computer?

ERIS is built to run for a whole company, either on its own hardware or hosted by Upward on its own servers in the Netherlands. According to its pricing page, a company with fewer than 10 staff can use a workstation of its own or Upward's server in the Netherlands.

How many users can ERIS have?

ERIS is priced as one licence and one price per user. The published pricing page sets the licence by company size, and the smallest companies pay per user only. The source material sets no fixed limit on users.
